findings.explanation: Splunkbase 3185 is the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft IIS, not a Proofpoint add-on. The link sends readers to the wrong product.
findings.quote: "title": "Splunkbase — Splunk Add-on for Proofpoint On Demand", "url": "https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/3185"
findings.suggested_fix: Point to the Proofpoint On Demand Email Security Add-on, https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4327 (TA-pps_ondemand).

findings.explanation: The published add-on for Proofpoint on Demand is 'Proofpoint On Demand Email Security Add-on' (folder `TA-pps_ondemand`, Splunkbase 4327), built by Proofpoint. `Splunk_TA_ProofpointOD` does not appear in the Splunkbase catalogue, and a Universal Forwarder cannot run this API-based collection.
findings.quote: Proofpoint On-Demand Add-on for Splunk (`Splunk_TA_ProofpointOD`) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
findings.suggested_fix: App: Proofpoint On Demand Email Security Add-on (`TA-pps_ondemand`, Splunkbase 4327), installed on a heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud IDM. Remove the UF reference from app, dataSources and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified even though its own implementation says field names must be validated, the sourcetype `proofpoint:filter` is not one the POD add-on documents, and the reference points to an unrelated add-on. No SME evidence supports the status.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft until the sourcetype, verdict fields and release/false-positive signal have been confirmed against a real POD feed.

findings.explanation: The POD add-on collects message and mail logs. I could not find a `proofpoint:filter` sourcetype; the add-on's documented sourcetypes appear to be `pps_messagelog`/`pps_maillog`. User and admin quarantine releases, the false-positive signal, are not part of filter verdict events.
findings.quote: `sourcetype=proofpoint:filter` spam and content filter verdict events including quarantine or bulk scores
findings.suggested_fix: Check the TA-pps_ondemand props.conf for the actual sourcetype names and the fields for spam/bulk scores (for example the filter modules' spam score) and quarantine release actions. Document where release events come from.

findings.explanation: The Proofpoint On Demand Email Security Add-on maps its message and mail logs to the CIM Email datamodel. Filtering verdicts fit Email.Filtering, so leaving CIM empty hides the normalised path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `Email` (Filtering dataset) to cimModels once the field mapping is confirmed.

findings.explanation: The UC trends how often the spam/content filter wrongly blocks legitimate mail. It has nothing to do with rewriting mail, threats or DLP.
findings.quote: We watch how Proofpoint treats and rewrites mail, so threats and DLP events line up with what the security team already sees in their console.
findings.suggested_fix: We track how often the spam filter wrongly holds back good email that people then have to ask to be released, so mail admins can see if a filter change made things worse.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no `entity` split, no ticket join and no baseline comparison; it outputs one daily average rate. The description and implementation describe a different detection from the one shipped.
findings.quote: Groups `avg_fp_rate` by `entity` each `1d`. ... (2) Join to service-desk tickets tagged email for ground truth. (3) Alert when FP rate exceeds baseline.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual output (daily FP-signal percentage over 30 days), or state the baseline rule and ticket correlation as follow-on steps not covered by the search.

findings.explanation: This is generic boilerplate. The SPL runs over -30d@d with no entity, and `host, user, action` are not the fields the search uses (verdict, false_positive, user_release, admin_override).
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity ... Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`host, user, action`).
findings.suggested_fix: Give POD-specific steps: configure the POD add-on's log API credentials (cluster ID and token), confirm verdict and release fields in the message log, schedule daily over -30d@d, and validate against the POD quarantine release report.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: It coalesces guessed fields (false_positive, user_release, admin_override, Verdict/Disposition) under an unconfirmed sourcetype `proofpoint:filter`. fp_rate_pct divides by all messages rather than by filtered messages, so it is not a filter false-positive rate, and `filtered` is computed but never used.
'IT Operations' paired with securityDomain 'soc_operations'. Spam filter tuning is usually owned by messaging or security operations; confirm the intended pillar.

summary: A spam-filter false-positive trend for Proofpoint On Demand, marked `verified`, but the add-on name and folder look invented and the reference links to the Microsoft IIS add-on. The sourcetype and fields are guesses the text itself admits ('field names vary by POD'), and the plain-language explanation describes a different use case.
